selection: Purposive adversarial precedent search, not a systematic or exhaustive census.

works.title: Out of Order: Understanding Repair and Maintenance
works.scope: Selected printed pp. 1–2, 4–8; PDF pp. 2–3, 5–9. Complete text extracted locally, not comprehensively reviewed.

observations.observation: Maintenance includes apprenticeship, improvisation and changes to objects; restoration need not return an identical object.
observations.claim_limit: Conceptual synthesis drawing on cited ethnographies; no reanalysis of those datasets here.

observations.observation: The authors already connect continuing urban provision with recurrent maintenance and explain its low visibility.
observations.claim_limit: A predecessor to the general maintenance insight, not a quantified ancient necessity theorem.

works.title: Beyond Markets and States: Polycentric Governance of Complex Economic Systems
works.publication_note: Nobel Prize lecture delivered 8 December 2009; official Les Prix Nobel witness, with printed pagination beginning at 408. Related 2010 AER version has different pagination.
works.scope: Selected printed pp. 411–412, 414 and 420; PDF pp. 4–5, 7 and 13.

observations.observation: The author retrospectively reports productive multi-agency metropolitan water arrangements and efficient autonomous direct-service producers, alongside some concentrated indirect services.
observations.claim_limit: Original water/police data and long archaeological durations were not reanalyzed.

observations.locus: Printed pp. 414 and 420 / PDF pp. 7 and 13
observations.observation: Models make precise assumptions; institution analysis also considers rights, information, aggregation and payoffs.
observations.claim_limit: These conditions must be investigated separately from aggregate physical feasibility.

works.title: Integrating Restoration and Scheduling Decisions for Disrupted Interdependent Infrastructure Systems
works.publication_note: Annals of Operations Research 203, 279–294; inspected author manuscript has 23 separately numbered pages.
works.scope: Manuscript pp. 1–4 and 7–11; author-page publication/abstract fields.

observations.observation: The model jointly selects repair tasks, assigns work groups and schedules service recovery over a horizon under dependencies.
observations.claim_limit: A direct predecessor for joint scheduling; its restored components remain available for the remaining horizon.

observations.observation: The author page distinguishes online-first September 2011 from journal issue March 2013.
observations.claim_limit: One work with two witnesses, not two independent precedents.

works.title: Capital, Volume II, chapter 20: Simple Reproduction
works.publication_note: Original volume date; exact online English translation edition not established from this witness.
works.scope: Section II, The Two Departments of Social Production, only. The HTML contains other sections that were not used.

observations.observation: The scheme separates means of production from consumption products and discusses fixed capital surviving annual wear.
observations.claim_limit: A capitalist reproduction theory; not a universal description of ancient production.

works.title: Modeling joint restoration strategies for interdependent infrastructure systems
works.scope: Selected abstract, introduction, Joint restoration strategy model, Model of restoration process, and rights notice. Case results were not reproduced.

observations.locus: Joint restoration strategy model; Model of restoration process
observations.observation: The paper models joint recovery sequences and losses through time and declares one-step repair of physical failures.
observations.claim_limit: A further restoration predecessor with substantive timing assumptions, not an ancient persistence test.

works.title: The persistence of ancient settlements and urban sustainability
works.scope: Europe PMC JATS XML sec s1, What Is Settlement Persistence?, selected first and final paragraphs.

observations.locus: JATS XML sec[@id="s1"], first and final paragraphs
observations.observation: The authors distinguish occupation, demographic, institutional and cultural persistence and question nominal continuity caused by modern labeling.
observations.claim_limit: Definitions and comparative design guidance; no new archaeological sample analyzed here.

works.title: Housing inequality and settlement persistence are associated across the archaeological record
works.scope: Europe PMC JATS XML sec s8, Settlement Persistence, paragraph 1; sec s3, first paragraph concerning dating resolution.

observations.observation: The coding measures substantial occupation episodes, separates abandonment/reoccupation and excludes ephemeral phases while allowing size change within an episode.
observations.claim_limit: A specific duration definition that can conceal contractions and expansions.

observations.observation: Different dating resolution can expose or miss short abandonments.
observations.claim_limit: The source notes a measurement issue; its full inequality dataset and regressions were not independently reproduced.
